{{Current events|year=2018|month=03|day=31|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Metropolitan Police Service|Police]] in [[London]] announce the arrest on March 29 of a 19-year-old man suspected of the commission, preparation, or instigation of acts of terrorism. [https://www.time1075.net/east-london-man-held-under-terrorism-act/ (Time 107.5fm)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Siege of Eastern Ghouta]], [[Rif Dimashq offensive (February 2018–present)]]
**The [[Syrian Army]] declares that the eastern [[Ghouta]] towns of [[Arbin, Syria|Arbin]], [[Zamalka]], [[Jobar]], and [[Ein Tarma]] are vacated of rebel fighters. Except for the town of [[Douma, Syria|Douma]], which is facing an ultimatum, the government controls most of the area around the capital [[Damascus]]. [http://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/news/article.cfm?c_id=2&objectid=12023968 (AP via ''The New Zealand Herald'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[General Conference (LDS Church)]]
**[[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] announces the elevation of Brazilian [[Ulisses Soares]] and [[Chinese Americans|Chinese American]] [[Gerrit W. Gong]] to the church's top leadership group, the [[Quorum of the Twelve Apostles (LDS Church)|Quorum of the Twelve Apostles]]. They are respectively the first Latin American and first man of Asian descent to serve in this role. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/mormon-conference-ushers-leaders-church-faces-scrutiny-050209721.html (AP via Yahoo!)]
**LDS [[President of the Church (LDS Church)|President]] [[Russell M. Nelson]] announces that [[High priest (Latter Day Saints)|High Priests]] [[Quorum (Latter Day Saints)|Quorum]] will be merged into [[Elder (Latter Day Saints)|Elders Quorum]]. [https://www.heraldextra.com/news/local/faith/historic-changes-to-priesthood-structure-announced-at-priesthood-session-of/article_219c400a-1b63-5faf-ae2a-3ffcc7e4e3b3.html (''Daily Herald'')]
*A man attempts [[Seppuku]] at [[Nankang Software Park]] in [[Taiwan]], apparently in response to the final public appearance of online celebrity Zhou 'Dora' Yingxin. [https://kotaku.com/man-attempts-suicide-after-internet-idols-retirement-1824276932 (Kotaku)]

;Disasters and accidents
*U.S.-based automobile manufacturer [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] confirms that one of their [[Tesla Model X|Model X]] cars was placed into Autopilot mode moments before a fatal crash in [[California]], [[United States]]. Tesla's Autopilot system is not intended to operate independently and as such the driver is meant to have their hands on the wheel at all times. The recorder of the system logged that the driver did not have their hands on the wheel at the time of the crash. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43604440 (BBC)]
*Updated analysis by the [[European Space Agency]] and [[Aerospace Corporation]] suggests that the derelict [[China|Chinese]] space station ''[[Tiangong-1]]'' will crash on tomorrow evening or the day thereafter in the morning. Although the prediction remains highly uncertain, the station may impact around [[Africa]]. [https://www.space.com/40163-chinese-space-station-crash-april-1-or-april-2.html (Space.com)]
*A fire destroys four [[World Food Programme]] warehouses in [[Hudaydah]], [[Yemen]], which contained 50 tonnes of food as well as fuel and mattresses. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-43606207 (BBC)]
*[[Stansted Airport]] in the [[United Kingdom]] reopens after a shuttle bus fire. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/mar/31/stansted-airport-flights-resume-after-shuttle-bus-fire (''The Guardian'')]
*In [[Japan]], [[Kyushu Electric Power]] shuts down their [[Genkai Nuclear Power Plant]] because of a steam leak less than a week after being restarted for the first time in seven years. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20180331/p2g/00m/0dm/002000c (''The Mainichi'')]
*An explosion at a market in [[Jalalabad]], [[Afghanistan]], kills one person and injures three others. [https://www.tolonews.com/afghanistan/two-wounded-jalalabad-explosion (Tolo News)]
*A bulldozer damages a gas line with a subsequent explosion at a construction site in [[Galala Mountain|al-Jalala mountain]], [[Egypt]], killing two people and wounding nine more. [http://www.egyptindependent.com/two-workers-killed-9-injured-jalala-mountain-gas-explosion/ (''The Egypt Independent'')]
*A hotel collapses in [[Indore]], [[India]], killing at least 10 people. [https://www.cnbc.com/2018/03/31/dozens-are-feared-trapped-after-a-hotel-collapses-in-india-reports.html (CNBC)]
*A fairground ride collapses in [[Neuville-sur-Saône]], central [[France]]. Occupied pods attached to the ride fall to the ground, ejecting some riders, with one man dead. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/frenchman-dies-after-fairground-ride-collapse-10092972 (Channel News Asia)]
*As workers attempt to clean up an oil spill, a fire breaks out off the coast of [[Borneo]] near [[Balikpapan]], [[Indonesia]], killing at least two fishermen. [[Search and rescue]] personnel evacuate all 20 crew from a nearby ship. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asiapacific/oil-spill-cleanup-fire-kills-2-in-indonesia-10092100 (AFP via Channel News Asia)]

;International relations
*[[Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] Foreign Office considers a consular request from the government of [[Russia]] for visitation with [[Yulia Skripal]], the daughter of poisoned ex-spy [[Sergei Skripal]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/mar/31/foreign-office-considers-russian-consular-access-to-yulia-skripal (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Malaysia]]n Maritime Enforcement Agency claims a [[Vietnam]]ese fishing vessel tried to ram one of their boats when they tried to detain it for illegally entering and fishing from Malaysian waters. [http://www.thesundaily.my/news/2018/03/31/vietnamese-fishing-boat-tries-ram-mmea-ship (''The Sun Daily'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]], [[2018 Land Day demonstration]]
**[[Palestinian Authority]] President [[Mahmoud Abbas]] accuses [[Israel]] of responsibility for the deaths of 16 protestors at the border with [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. Israel accuses Palestinian terrorists of using civilians as human shields. A video begins circulating on [[social media]] appearing to show an unarmed teenager being shot. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-03-31/palestinians-seek-protection-as-israel-blasts-terrorist-march (Bloomberg)]
**Israel claims to have identified ten of the dead as members of terrorist organisations, and publishes a list of their names and the groups Israel says they belonged to. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-at-least-10-of-the-16-killed-at-gaza-border-were-members-of-terror-groups/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*An unknown source supposedly leaks a report from the [[Germany|German]] defence ministry which suggests the nation's Tornado fighter jets may not meet [[NATO]] requirements for secure encrypted communications and are therefore potentially unsuitable for NATO missions. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-germany-military-fighter-jet/german-tornado-jet-may-be-unsuitable-for-nato-missions-report-idUKKBN1H70E6?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[France|French]] ambassador to [[Italy]] is summoned to the [[Italy|Italian]] foreign ministry to explain an incident in which French police cross over the sovereign border of Italy, enter a migrant clinic in [[Turin]], and force a refugee to take a [[Clinical urine tests|urine test]]. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43606225 (BBC)]
*In order to make sea room for expanding berthing facilities in [[Trincomalee Harbour]], the [[Sri Lanka]]n navy raises the SS ''Sagaing'', a [[United Kingdom|British]] passenger ship sunk when it was bombed in an April 1942 [[Japan]]ese air strike during [[World War II]]. [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-43607838 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in Russia]]
**The Russian [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Russia)|Ministry of Internal Affairs]] detains [[Ziyavudin Magomedov]], his brother [[Magomed Magomedov]], and the chief executive of the Summa Group on charges of embezzlement of public funds and criminal association. A [[Moscow]] court orders Ziyavudin Magomedov, one of the [[List of Russian people by net worth|richest Russians]], to remain in pre-trial custody until May 30. [http://tass.com/society/997067 (TASS)], [https://www.reuters.com/article/russia-summa-detention/russian-tycoon-magomedov-to-stay-in-pre-trial-custody-until-may-idUSR4N1RC004 (Reuters)]
*[[Human rights in Turkey]]
**The [[Law Society of England and Wales]] issues a report claiming that [[Turkey]] has prosecuted 1,539 lawyers since the [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|2016 coup d'état attempt]]. The report states that 580 people still remain incarcerated with 103 more having received prison sentences. [https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/news/turkeys-arrested-lawyers-103-jailed-for-long-sentences/5065464.article (''The Law Gazette'')]
*In [[Madarganj Upazila]], [[Jamalpur]], [[Bangladesh]], a group of between 70 and 80 people from one faith of mosque attack an inauguration ceremony for another faith of mosque, resulting in at least 20 injured. [https://www.rabwah.net/ahmadiyya-mosque-attacked-in-bangladesh/ (''The Rabwah Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Sierra Leonean general election, 2018]]
**The second round of a general election begins in [[Sierra Leone]] with a tight race expected between the [[Sierra Leone People's Party|People's Party]] and the [[All People's Congress]]. Incumbent [[President of Sierra Leone|President]] [[Ernest Bai Koroma]] is constitutionally barred from seeking a third term in office. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/mar/31/sierra-leone-presidential-runoff-election-voting-begins (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Botswana]]n [[President of Botswana|President]] [[Ian Khama]] steps down and hands power over to Vice President [[Mokgweetsi Masisi]]. [http://www.africanews.com/2018/03/31/botswana-president-ian-khama-steps-down-after-end-of-tenure/ (Africa News)]

;Science and technology
*The current largest [[cruise ship]] in the world [[Royal Caribbean International]]'s [[United States dollar|$]]1.35 billion [[Symphony of the Seas|MV ''Symphony of the Seas'']] commences its [[maiden voyage]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/travel/cruises/2018/03/31/symphony-seas-worlds-largest-cruise-ship-kicks-off-maiden-voyage/475464002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Sports
*[[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]]
**The [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]] and the [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova Wildcats]] advance to the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|National Championship Game]] after defeating the [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola Ramblers]] and [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas Jayhawks]] in the Final Four. [https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2018-final-four-villanova-vs-michigan-to-play-for-ncaa-championship/ (CBS Sports)]
